Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Technologies Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud Technologies's results for the Q3 FY2024. With me on the call are Raj Patel, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Product Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud Technologies delivered another strong Q3, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

Let me highlight our overall financial performance, which really underscores another quarter of robust execution in a dynamic cloud landscape. We're outpacing the industry by capitalizing on accelerating AI workloads, enterprise multi-cloud migrations, and edge computing expansions. Diving into the key metrics, we posted Q3 revenue of $28.7 billion, up 19% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, beating our guidance midpoint and consensus by $400 million. This is our 15th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth, powered by a 31% surge in AI/ML services revenue, which now makes up 22% of total revenue—rising from 14% last year. Core Infrastructure-as-a-Service grew 17% year-over-year to $18.2 billion, thanks to compute utilization rates averaging 78%, while Platform-as-a-Service and SaaS offerings, like our Nebula AI Platform and QuantumForge database services, leaped 25% to $10.5 billion.

Annual Recurring Revenue hit $112 billion, with net revenue retention at an impressive 118%, showing strong expansion among our top 1,000 customers. On profitability, we recorded GAAP operating income of $10.1 billion, with a 35.2% operating margin—expanding 210 basis points year-over-year to our highest ever. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 38.5%, aided by $1.2 billion in cost optimizations across data centers, including our next-gen Graviton4 ARM-based instances that cut customer compute costs by 25% and lifted our margins.

Net income came in at $8.4 billion, or $1.72 diluted EPS, up 22% year-over-year. Free cash flow was outstanding at $12.3 billion, or 45% of revenue, backed by $7.5 billion in operating cash flow. We finished the quarter with $85 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable securities, giving us plenty of firepower for our $50 billion multi-year capex plan aimed at AI hyperscale data centers.

Regionally, growth was balanced: Americas at 62% of revenue with $17.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year, driven by U.S. public sector deals like a $2.5 billion multi-year DoD contract for secure sovereign cloud services. EMEA contributed 22% or $6.3 billion, up 23%, accelerating with GDPR-aligned data residency zones and telco partnerships like Vodafone for 5G edge. APAC was 16% or $4.6 billion, up 21%, led by 28% growth in Japan and 35% in India, where Mumbai and Tokyo regions reached full utilization for clients like Toyota and Reliance Industries. Emerging markets drove 12% of new bookings, up from 8%, via alliances with Alibaba Cloud and Tencent for hybrid interoperability.

Key trends fueling this include AI/ML hyperscale, where AetherML inference revenue doubled year-over-year, with migrations to Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing; edge services up 45% to $2.1 billion via Outpost appliances in over 5,000 sites; and sustainability with PUE at 1.15. We're gaining share in AI workloads to 32% per Canalys, countering competitors with 20% cheaper spot instances. These results affirm our AI Everywhere strategy, with $18 billion Q4 capex for 20 new AI zones and $9 billion returned to shareholders. For Q4, we guide revenue to $29.5-30.0 billion, 19-21% growth; FY2024 full-year $114-115 billion.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Raj. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue increased by 19% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 68.2%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 35.2%.

Let me delve deeper into our overall gross margin trends and the drivers propelling them forward, as this is central to our profitability in the competitive cloud space. In Q3, consolidated gross margin hit 68.2%, up 250 basis points year-over-year and 110 sequentially, marking 11 straight quarters of expansion for a trailing four-quarter average of 67.5%—ahead of peers like AWS around 32%, Azure mid-60s, and Google Cloud sub-60%. Non-GAAP gross margin was 69.8%, excluding stock comp and amortization.

Breaking it down by pillars across our $28.7 billion revenue: Product mix shifted favorably, with PaaS and SaaS at 62% of revenue, up from 55%, driven by AI/ML via Aether AI Foundry growing 145% to represent 22%. These high-margin services exceed 82% gross margins due to software focus. IaaS improved to 58% from 54%, aided by pricing discipline. This mix shift added about 150 basis points year-over-year. Enterprise migrations to generative AI cut their TCO by 30-40%, boosting our ARPU.

Infrastructure efficiency boosted utilization to 85% from 78%, via Aether Orchestrator, lowering compute COGS 18%. Nexara Graviton-X chips—third-gen ARM silicon in 65% of capacity—offer 25% better price-performance, 40% less power, adding 200 basis points post-$2.1 billion capex amortization. Energy efficiency: 75% renewables cut electricity COGS 12%; PUE at 1.12 vs. industry 1.5.

Regionally: North America 70.1% margins up 300 bps; EMEA 66.8%; APAC 62.4% despite 120% growth; Rest of World 64.2%. $1.2 billion capex traded margins for RPO growth to $185 billion. Headwinds like 8% bandwidth from AI data and supply inflation were offset by contracts and Nvidia diversification. Q4 margins guided 68.5-69.0%; full-year 68.8%. Catalysts: Edge Cloud 20% uplift, Snowflake integrations, capex at 18% of revenue.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation AetherCloud platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

Today, I'd like to highlight our advancements in security and compliance certifications, a key differentiator fueling 28% year-over-year growth in enterprise bookings from regulated sectors like finance, healthcare, and government. In Q3, we secured FedRAMP High Authorization for AetherCore IaaS and Kubernetes Engine, opening federal opportunities with 45% QoQ pipeline growth and $75 million ARR from initial contracts. This elite status, with 20-30% lower TCO, positions us with AWS GovCloud and Azure Government.

In EU, ISO 27001:2022 covers all EMEA zones including Frankfurt and Paris, aligning with GDPR and EU Data Act; IRAP PROTECTED in Australia unlocked $50 million defense deals. EMEA drove 35% workloads from DAX 40 banks; APAC 52% bookings. Healthcare: Renewed expanded HIPAA/HITECH and HITRUST CSF r2 across all services including Aether Sage, zero major findings in 1,200+ controls; healthcare ARR up 41% to $320 million.

Technical initiatives: Zero-Trust Architecture at 100% via Aether Sentinel, MTTD under 5 minutes vs. industry 17; Quantum-Resistant Cryptography with 85% migration to Kyber/Dilithium in HSMs; Compliance Copilot automates 70% audits, cutting time 60%, passing SOC 2 Type II on 14,000+ controls for multi-cloud. These drive 68% ARR from certified workloads, up from 52%; NPS 78 vs. 55 industry; 92% gross retention, 135% NRR. Ahead: PCI DSS 4.0 Q4, CSA STAR Level 3. Security spend at 18% CAGR fortifies our moat.

Now, I'll pass it over to Mike Chen for a product roadmap update.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We are excited about the market reception to our new Nebula AI Platform offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the AI/ML sector.

I'll focus now on our customer churn rate and retention trends, vital for long-term value as lifetime value stems from sticky workloads and expansions. Our north star is net revenue retention, or NRR. In Q3 FY2024, NRR was 119%, flat sequentially but up 200 basis points year-over-year from 117%, beating peers' 110-115% per Bessemer benchmarks. Gross dollar retention hit 92%, up 150 basis points, 11th straight gain.

Logo churn was 1.8%, down from 2.2%; revenue-weighted 1.2%, annualizing to 7-8% vs. industry 10-12%. Zero churn in top 100 customers. Enterprise (> $100K ARR) NRR 125% with 25% upsell from Graviton and managed Spark; commercial/SMB 108%, churn 3.5% from dev/test rationalization. IaaS 115% NRR; PaaS 132%; AI/ML 45% expansion.

Americas (55% ARR) 1.0% churn, 122% NRR; EMEA (30%) 1.5% from 2.3%, GDPR zones key; APAC (15%) 3.2% down 400 bps, 110% NRR with Singapore/NTT investments. Drivers: Customer Success 2.0 AI FinOps cuts involuntary churn 30%; multi-cloud Outposts neutralizes poaching; agentic AI orchestration boosts expansions 15%; GPU spot marketplace at 85% utilization. Contractual guardrails cover 70% enterprise ARR. Q4 NRR 118-120%, churn <1.7%. This supports 25%+ growth vs. 20% market CAGR.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Moreno to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Mike. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

A key area of focus has been navigating the impact of currency fluctuations on our global revenue, especially with over 65% of our $28.7 billion Q3 revenue from outside the U.S., exposing us to FX volatility like peers AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Currency created a 4.2% headwind, or $760 million drag; constant currency growth was 28% vs. reported 24%. DXY up 5.8% QoQ from U.S. yields and geopolitics.

EMEA 52% of impact ($395 million), euro down 6.2%, pound 4.9%; EMEA revenue €4.1 billion (38%) 7% higher constant euro, pressure on sovereign clouds. APAC 28% ($215 million), yen -7.1%, AUD -3.4%; Japan 32% constant growth on GPUs. LATAM 20% ($150 million), BRL -8.3%, MXN -5.2% on SaaS. Mirrors AWS 4% headwind.

Mitigations: Hedging covers 75% 12-month transactional, 60% 24-month translation, gaining $280 million Q2; dynamic pricing in 14 currencies preserves margins; local-currency billing in new zones. FY2024 FX 3-5% headwind if DXY 105-107. Building resilience: Edge with Nokia for LATAM; grow non-USD to 70% by FY2026 via AI subscriptions less elastic. Underlying 31% constant growth, margins up 210 bps to 32.4%.

Back to Raj Patel.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

To wrap up, let's discuss Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, our key metric for future revenue visibility in our subscription model—current RPO within 12 months, non-current beyond. Total RPO ended Q3 at $48.7 billion, up 31% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, 11th straight 30%+ quarter. Current RPO $19.8 billion, +27%; non-current $28.9 billion, +34%. Coverage 2.4x trailing revenue, implying $40 billion+ over 24 months pre-upsell; cohorts grow 22% year one.

AI supercharges: $750 million five-year bank deal for AetherVector LLMs; NVIDIA/Hugging Face add 15% Q3 RPO; AetherEdge +45%. Americas 52% ($25.3 billion +32%); EMEA $13.2 billion (+30%) sovereign wins; APAC $10.2 billion (+35%). AetherOne bundles lock capacity, churn <5%; $2.5 billion capex for liquid-cooled H100s. Guides FY2024 $22.5-23.0 billion (28% growth), FY2025 30%+. Diversified base mitigates risks.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. Raj, can you elaborate on the AI workload acceleration and how it's impacting gross margins long-term? Specifically, with the mix shift to higher-margin PaaS, do you see any risk of GPU supply constraints pressuring that trajectory?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, John. Great question. Our AI momentum is real, with 31% growth in that segment reflecting hyperscale migrations and new deals like the DoD sovereign cloud. The product mix shift to PaaS/AI at 62% is a tailwind, contributing 150 basis points to margin expansion, as these services run above 82%. On GPUs, we've diversified beyond H100s with in-house alternatives and spot instances, keeping utilization high at 85%. Supply chains are de-risked via $50 billion capex, so no major pressure—expect continued 200+ bps expansion into FY2025 as efficiencies scale.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, thanks. Sarah, on the FX headwind and RPO strength—how much of the 31% RPO growth is from multi-year AI deals, and do you expect currency to moderate in Q4 with potential Fed cuts?

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, Emily. About 65% of new ACV bookings were three-plus year terms, heavily weighted to AI like AetherTensor v2.0 and vector DBs, driving non-current RPO +34% to $28.9 billion. Regional balance with APAC +35% shows resilience. FX was 4.2% drag this quarter; hedges offset 37%, and with DXY possibly peaking, we see 3-5% for FY2024. Dynamic pricing and local billing will help—constant currency underpins our Q4 guide.

Raj Patel:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
